scenes.label: THE BED
lines: Why are hotel beds almost always white?

Why are hotel beds
almost always *white?*
There's a story, and a practical reason.

There's a *story,* and a
*practical reason.*
In August nineteen ninety-nine, Westin introduced its all-white Heavenly Bed.

In *1999*, Westin introduced
its all-white *Heavenly Bed.*
Other chains answered by upgrading their own beds.

Other chains *upgraded*
their own beds.

scenes.label: THE LOOK
lines: Westin is credited with popularising the all-white look in hotels.

Westin is credited with
popularising *all-white.*
It didn't invent white sheets, but it made the white bed famous.

It didn't *invent* white sheets.
It made them *famous.*

scenes.label: WHY WHITE
lines: White tells guests, at a glance, that the bed is clean.

White says *clean,*
*at a glance.*
And white linen can be bleached, so it comes back looking new.

It can be *bleached,* so it
comes back *looking new.*

scenes.label: FOR HOSPITALITY
lines: For hospitality, it's a reminder: guests judge clean with their eyes first.

Guests judge *clean*
with their *eyes first.*
What guests can see is part of what they trust.

What guests *see* is part
of what they *trust.*
Follow Qarya, for more hospitality literacy.

Follow Qarya for more
*Hospitality Literacy.*
